name: Performance Optimization
description: Performance — lazy loading, memoization, caching strategies, bundle size, database indexing, efficient algorithms
content:
# Performance Optimization Guidelines

- Lazy-load non-critical resources — use code splitting, dynamic imports, and `React.lazy()` (or framework equivalent) to defer loading until needed
- Memoize expensive computations — use `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `functools.lru_cache`, or similar patterns to avoid redundant calculations
- Implement caching at every layer — browser cache (Cache-Control headers), CDN, application cache (Redis/Memcached), and database query cache
- Monitor and minimize bundle size — use tree shaking, analyze bundles with tools like webpack-bundle-analyzer, and avoid importing entire libraries for single functions
- Add database indexes on columns used in WHERE, JOIN, and ORDER BY clauses — use `EXPLAIN` to verify query plans and identify full table scans
- Choose appropriate data structures and algorithms — prefer O(1) lookups (hash maps) over O(n) scans, and avoid nested loops on large datasets
- Debounce and throttle user input handlers — search inputs, scroll handlers, and resize listeners should not fire on every event
- Optimize images and media — use modern formats (WebP, AVIF), responsive sizes (`srcset`), and lazy loading for below-the-fold content
- Use pagination or virtual scrolling for large lists — never render thousands of DOM elements at once
- Measure before optimizing — use profiling tools (Chrome DevTools, flamegraphs, APM) to identify actual bottlenecks rather than guessing
